args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions and is healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open.

- **Rollback:** The bad release was v2.3.1, with an 18% error rate in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. A later status check shows all three regions on v2.3.0, the service healthy and the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged on-call. It says what failed, what I rolled back to, the results after the rollback, and that the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again.

The release candidate for v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging before it went to production. The incident mentions this too.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
